followUps: Require expected old text for optimistic patching.
followUpGuide: For line and column coordinates, precompute line start offsets and convert each edit to a character range before validation.
For expected old text, validate that `text[start:end]` matches the edit's expected value before applying any replacements.

For multi-file patches, validate every file and every edit first, then build all new contents before writing any result. This prevents partial application of invalid edits, but filesystem writes can still fail halfway through. True multi-file atomicity needs a transaction or a staging/commit/rollback design, plus a check that source versions haven't changed.
complexityAnalysis: - Sorting edits. Time: O(e log e), where e is edit count. Space: O(e) for sorted edits.
- Validation. Time: O(e). Space: O(1) beyond sorted edits.
- Python's left-to-right list/join builder. Time: O(n + total replacement size + e); extra space: O(n + total replacement size + e). Here n is original text length. Sorting adds O(e log e).

- A right-to-left mutable string builder preserves offsets but may shift its suffix on every replacement. The provided Java approach can take O(e · (n + total replacement size)) work in the worst case. Use a left-to-right append builder for a linear construction phase.
solutionGuide: Sort and validate first. Build the result with a piece list so total work stays linear in text plus replacements.
